# Go Fundamentals: Intro

Welcome to Go! Go is an open source programming language supported by Google with clean syntax, built-in concurrency, and fast compilation.

## Further information

- [fmt.Println — Go Standard Library](https://pkg.go.dev/fmt#Println)
- [A Tour of Go: Packages](https://go.dev/tour/basics/1)
- [Go by Example: Hello World](https://gobyexample.com/hello-world)
instructions: Fix the greeting so it prints "Hello, Golanger!" to stdout using fmt.Println.
hint: Import "fmt" and call `fmt.Println("Hello, Golanger!")` inside main().

references.title: fmt.Println — Go Standard Library
references.description: Official package documentation for fmt.Println and standard output functions.

references.title: A Tour of Go: Packages
references.description: Introduction to Go programs, package structure, and main function.

references.title: Go by Example: Hello World
references.description: Classic starter program with execution walkthrough.

# Variables & Constants

Go is statically typed. Variables can be declared using `var`, short declaration `:=`, or `const` for immutable compile-time constants.

## Further information

- [Variable Declarations — Go Language Specification](https://go.dev/ref/spec#Variable_declarations)
- [A Tour of Go: Variables](https://go.dev/tour/basics/8)
- [Go by Example: Variables](https://gobyexample.com/variables)
instructions: Declare a variable `x` of type int with value 42 using the `var` keyword.
hint: Syntax: `var x int = 42`

references.title: Variable Declarations — Go Language Specification
references.description: Official grammar and semantics for the var declaration keyword in Go.

references.title: A Tour of Go: Variables
references.description: Interactive introduction to package-level and function-level var statements.

references.title: Go by Example: Variables
references.description: Demonstrations of declaring variables with var and zero values.

Go types include `int`, `float64`, `string`, `bool`. Go does NOT perform implicit type conversions—all numeric conversions must be explicit.

hint: Types: int64, float32, byte.
